page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-192GB is a memory-rich virtual instance within the Cloud Native family, powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 32 shared vCPUs mapped to AMD EPYC 7542 processors operating at a nominal clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The system provides 192 GB of total system RAM, establishing an allocation of 6.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware instruction support includes AVX, AES-NI, and SHA-NI, while AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The configuration does not include local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent disks, and includes no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel throughput alongside modest baseline single-core performance. In Geekbench testing, the server scores 2,035 in single-core and 18,078 in multi-core metrics, alongside a top-tier ray tracing score of 50,932. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 234.59 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile of tested machines. Conversely, stress-ng single-core execution registers in the bottom decile at 750.49, reflecting shared-core multi-tenant CPU allocation and conservative base clocking. Memory throughput remains balanced, delivering 125.11 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth and 55.14 GB/sec write bandwidth.

This server type offers solid resource density for multi-threaded and memory-heavy workloads that do not demand dedicated CPU cores or low-latency local NVMe disks. Suitable deployments include large in-memory caching tiers such as Redis, batch processing pipelines, static web serving infrastructure, staging database instances, and parallel compilation tasks.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-32xCPU-192GB is a virtual server instance powered by AMD EPYC 7542 processors running on the KVM hypervisor. Configured with 32 shared vCPUs at 2.0 GHz and 192 GB of RAM (6.0 GB per core), it provides a high-density memory profile without bundled local storage or dedicated graphics hardware. Across performance benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong multi-threaded capabilities, achieving 18,078 in Geekbench multi-core and 234.59 GB/sec in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, while single-core synthetic stress scores remain lower due to shared resource allocation. Memory bandwidth registers at 125.11 GB/sec for large read operations. The instance serves multi-threaded, memory-intensive workloads including in-memory datastores, background ETL processing, static web traffic handling, and CI/CD build environments requiring large memory footprints.
